name: Ida
label: Simple Machines
lede: Daniel Littleton left Annapolis hardcore behind and started singing quietly with Elizabeth Mitchell, and Simple Machines put out the tapes. Three albums later, Ida was the label's gentlest band.

eras.title: A cassette recorder and a lot of quiet
eras.text: Daniel Littleton walked out of Annapolis hardcore and into a room with Elizabeth Mitchell, a guitar and a cassette recorder. What came out was hushed and homemade, and nothing like what he had played before.

years.h: Annapolis hardcore singer Daniel Littleton turns the volume down
years.p: [[Daniel Littleton|54a0c6a1-08bc-464d-be5d-1f571ad932e7]], who fronted the Annapolis band [[The Hated|44a38273-7da3-433e-8213-554452f6f9bd]], starts writing with [[Elizabeth Mitchell|03845f1b-b6bd-426a-b163-04b347e45270]]. The first Ida tapes are "super lo-fi", made for friends.
years.xp:
Chronogram has the two meeting in 1990 through a mutual friend in Boston and becoming a couple in 1991. Mitchell, then a Brown student, took a job teaching nursery school in Brooklyn, and Littleton followed her there.

The Hated was part of the first wave of 1980s hardcore, per Littleton's podcast interview. Ida kept two voices, acoustic guitars and a lot of space between the notes.

years.h: A DC benefit with Ian MacKaye on the bill is Ida's first show out of town
years.p: Ida plays its first date outside New York in 1993, a benefit in Washington, close to the punk scene Littleton came from.
years.xp: Chronogram says the bill included [[Ian MacKaye|c12f644b-1066-4ead-b0dd-d0c380f5cca2]] and Mark Robinson. Ida's first local shows in New York had come the same year.

years.h: Jenny Toomey hears the cassette and offers a record
years.p: After shows with double-bassist Rick Lassiter, the band records a 4-track cassette. [[Jenny Toomey|246fc8dd-a667-4a5b-868a-a5897bcd6c59]] of Simple Machines hears it and offers to put out an album.
years.xp:
Toomey was the one who pushed the pair to play out in the first place, Chronogram reports. Simple Machines was the Arlington, Virginia label she ran with Kristin Thomson, known for its DIY tour manuals and for bands like [[Tsunami|fea43e99-c4d5-4dac-9c27-868e864c6dc2]] and [[Circus Lupus|01b418b2-5e47-4ce2-9144-ad7d35214103]].

Toomey also made the electro-pop record Listening Cap with Littleton as Liquorice (4AD, 1995).

eras.title: The Arlington label's gentlest band
eras.text: Three albums and a run of seven-inches for Simple Machines. By I Know About You, critics were reaching for words like harmonies and pretty.

years.h: Mitchell and Littleton play on a number-one single
years.p: They back [[Lisa Loeb|22c5cef9-80e8-48d2-acd3-6d16f6c8a16d]] on "Stay (I Missed You)", the single from the Reality Bites soundtrack that tops the chart in 1994.

years.h: Simple Machines puts out Tales of Brave Ida
years.p: Mostly the duo on record, then a fuller band live once Daniel's brother Michael "Miggy" Littleton joins on drums.
years.xp: Wikipedia dates the album to 1994; Chronogram says 1995. Michael Littleton became the band's drummer and multi-instrumentalist soon after, and stayed until 1999.

years.src: Wikipedia: I Know About You · Wikipedia: Ida (band)
yt: Downtown, live at Levon Helm Studios, 2025
years.h: The Chicago Tribune hears no better harmonies than Ida's
years.p: Its line on I Know About You: "No one has harmonies as beautiful as Ida." Alternative Press gives the album five stars.
years.xp:
Strings and upright bass sit under the two voices: Cecilia Littleton Bonner plays viola and violin, and Rick Lassiter plays upright bass and writes the string arrangements. Michael Littleton is on drums and Rose Thomson on bass.

"When I Was Now" is a cover of a Cindy Kallet song, the only one on the record. The Village Voice called it the best Ida album; Trouser Press found it "gentle, understated but fully inhabited."

years.h: Karla Schickele, daughter of Peter Schickele, joins on bass
years.p: [[Karla Schickele|cd341b7e-2628-49ee-8138-6177c96a0e9f]], who leads Beekeeper, becomes a permanent member and stays for the rest of the band's run.
years.xp: Wikipedia says she joined in late 1996; Chronogram says 1997. She is a Woodstock native, went on to record solo as k, and co-founded the Willie Mae Rock and Roll Camp for Girls in Brooklyn.

years.h: Ten Small Paces ends the Simple Machines run
years.p: The third and last Ida album for the label, and the first with Schickele in the line-up.
years.xp: One track, "Ashokan Reservoir", was recorded at night in the Catskills woods, per Chronogram.

eras.title: Strings come in, Capitol goes out
eras.text: Violin, cello and clarinet joined the folk core, and Ida got filed under chamber pop. A major label signed the band and let it go, and the record people remember came out on Tiger Style.

yt: Live at the Horseshoe Tavern, Toronto, 9/23/98
years.h: Ida takes two EPs and a string section on the road
years.p: Losing True and The Ida Retsin Family come out between albums. On tour, violinist Ida Pearle, cellist Elaine Ahn and clarinetist Sue Havens play alongside the band.

years.h: Michael Littleton leaves the drums in the year his brother marries Mitchell
years.p: Drummer [[Michael Littleton|c24f60a1-3cc1-4e22-bcc2-d38d9b105d87]] departs for White Magic and [[Blood on the Wall|8e4c8cc7-b5af-4329-a7ca-3d92c3a9ddb7]]. Daniel Littleton and Elizabeth Mitchell marry the same year.

years.big: "We wanted to see what would happen if we took a chance on a major label."
years.h: Capitol Records signs Ida, then lets them walk with the tapes
years.p: Daniel Littleton on the Capitol deal. The band records about three albums' worth, and leaves when the label restructures.
years.xp:
Littleton told Strand Magazine they wanted "the budget and the resources to record in great rooms." Then, he said, "the people who believed in us at Capitol eventually left, and suddenly the environment changed."

Allies inside the label helped Ida out of the contract and let it keep the master tapes, which Littleton called "an incredibly rare and mostly unheard of thing." He says the band released all of it independently.

years.h: Will You Find Me lands on Tiger Style and on the year-end lists
years.p: Spin and The New York Times both name it one of the year's best records. The New Yorker and the Village Voice praise it too.
years.xp: The Numero Group later reissued the album as a four-LP set, which is why Ida got back on stage in 2023.

years.cap: Ida as a four-piece by a lake; Elizabeth Mitchell in the pink top
years.h: Ida brings in strings and its fullest arrangements yet
years.p: A wider band now fills out the sound around Littleton, Mitchell and Schickele.

years.h: The Braille Night adds upright bass and violin
years.p: Zach Mitchell's upright bass and Ida Pearle's violin join the line-up around the record.

years.h: Storey is born, and Ida slows down
years.p: Storey Littleton is born to Mitchell and Daniel Littleton. The family leaves Brooklyn for Providence and then Woodstock, and the band goes quiet for a stretch.

eras.title: Up the Hudson, into a barn
eras.text: Ida moved to Woodstock and made its most rooted records, one of them in Levon Helm's studio. Mitchell built a second career in children's music, and the band stopped in 2010.

years.h: Ida settles in Woodstock
years.p: After Brooklyn and Providence, Mitchell and Littleton land in the Hudson Valley for good.
years.xp: Within two years they were playing Levon Helm's Midnight Ramble sessions in Woodstock, Chronogram reports, backing Michael Hurley.

years.h: Heart Like a River goes pastoral on Polyvinyl
years.p: A quieter, more stripped-down record. Violinist Jean Cook and drummer Ruth Keating join around it.
years.xp: Littleton described the approach as pastoral and stripped back, with the focus on the space between the sounds.

years.h: Jean Cook, of the Mekons, and drummer Ruth Keating join
years.p: [[Jean Cook|c304c9c2-e3f3-4abb-b7ca-61f86f4889f5]] and Ruth Keating fill out the Woodstock line-up.

years.h: Lovers Prayers gets made in Levon Helm's barn
years.p: Recorded at [[Levon Helm|392baa89-ea47-4de6-8dc0-fdac3ec85509]]'s studio in Woodstock, with Helm and folk singer [[Michael Hurley|a45bbcf5-f009-49cb-962e-4591083573d1]] on the record.
years.xp:
Littleton told Chronogram that "Playing with Michael was a huge thrill," and said of Helm: "Levon just knows how to make anything sound better."

Ida had played Helm's Midnight Ramble shows before making the record there.

years.cap: Ida's shadows on a screen above amps and guitars, Brattle Theatre, Cambridge
years.h: Ida plays NPR's Bryant Park Project
years.p: The band performs on the show, and its songs turn up on This American Life.

years.h: Ida Con Snock, with Michael Hurley, comes out on Gnomonsong
years.p: The label is co-owned by Devendra Banhart and Andy Cabic. The EP My Fair, My Dark arrives around the same time.
years.xp: The Hurley sessions were recorded alongside Lovers Prayers. Chronogram lists My Fair, My Dark as an August 2008 Polyvinyl EP.

years.cap: Elizabeth Mitchell and her band, daughter Storey in front
years.h: Ida goes quiet as Mitchell turns to children's music
years.p: Mitchell keeps going as a children's-music artist on Smithsonian Folkways. Littleton moves to free improvisation.

eras.title: The reissue calls them back
eras.text: A Numero Group reissue of Will You Find Me pulled the band out of retirement and onto a tour with its old Simple Machines labelmates.

years.cap: Ida at the Bowery Ballroom, New York
years.h: Ida plays again at Numero Twenty in Los Angeles
years.p: First show in over a decade, at the Numero Group's anniversary night, tied to its four-LP reissue of Will You Find Me.
years.xp:
Numero had asked Littleton for years about reissuing The Hated's catalog. He held out until the death of the original drummer: "I didn't want someone else deciding what happened to our history."

The Numero Twenty night put the original members back together, and daughter Storey, now a recording artist herself, played to the crowd.

years.cap: Ida at the Bowery Ballroom, New York, March 2025
years.h: Ida and Tsunami flip a coin to see who opens
years.p: On the Coin Toss Tour, the two Simple Machines bands settle each night's order with a coin and take audience questions.
years.xp: Littleton told Strand Magazine the Q&As ran from music to politics to everyday life.

sources.title: Strand Magazine: interview with Daniel Littleton
